skill.name: chatkit-botbuilder
skill.description: Build ChatKit chatbot implementations with OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP tool wrappers, FastAPI backends, Next.js frontends, and user isolation patterns.
skill.summary: Build ChatKit chatbot architectures with FastAPI, OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP tools, and user isolation guidance.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code examples, inline backticks, localhost URLs, and ordinary architecture terms. The confirmed security issue is guidance that places an OpenAI API key in frontend public configuration, with additional semantic concerns around browser token storage and development test-token bypasses. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: OpenAI API key is shown as a NEXT_PUBLIC frontend variable.
remediation.suggestion: Remove NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY from frontend examples. Keep OpenAI API keys only in backend environment variables and proxy any required calls through authenticated server endpoints.

remediation.issue: JWT bearer tokens are stored in localStorage and sessionStorage examples.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies or another token handling design with explicit XSS mitigations and short-lived access tokens.

remediation.issue: Development test-token authentication shortcut could be copied into production.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the shortcut from production examples or guard it with compile-time or deployment-only controls that cannot be enabled by user-controlled configuration.

remediation.issue: Some examples return raw exception messages to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Return generic client-facing errors and log detailed exceptions server-side with sensitive values redacted.

semantic_findings.title: Frontend OpenAI API Key Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The documentation recommends NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY in frontend configuration. In Next.js, NEXT_PUBLIC values are exposed to the browser, so copying this guidance can leak an OpenAI API key.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exact variable name appears in frontend environment guidance and includes an sk-style placeholder in the detailed integration guide. The risk follows directly from Next.js public environment variable behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Storage for Bearer Tokens
semantic_findings.description: The frontend examples read and write JWT bearer tokens in localStorage and sessionStorage. This pattern can expose sessions to XSS and should be replaced or mitigated for production deployments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited snippets explicitly store and retrieve access tokens from browser storage. This is a known session handling risk, although some applications may accept it with strong XSS controls.

semantic_findings.title: Development Test Token Bypass Pattern
semantic_findings.description: The backend example accepts bearer tokens that start with test-token when the environment is development. This is acceptable for local testing but can become an authentication bypass if the environment gate is misconfigured.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bypass is explicitly scoped to development, so malicious intent is not evident. The pattern is still risky guidance because a copied or misconfigured deployment could accept forged user IDs.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable patterns for connecting ChatKit to real application workflows. This skill provides architecture guidance for FastAPI backends, MCP tools, Next.js widgets, and user isolation.
actual_capabilities: Explains a FastAPI ChatKit server architecture with streaming responses.
Shows how to wrap MCP tools so user_id is injected into tool calls.
Provides Next.js ChatKit widget configuration with authenticated fetch examples.
Documents user isolation checks across middleware, tools, and database queries.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for ChatKit endpoints, tokens, and synchronization.
Describes deployment considerations for domain keys, CORS, and environment variables.
limitations: Provides documentation and snippets, not a complete runnable application in this package.
Some referenced template and asset folders are not present in the submitted files.
Examples must be adapted to the current ChatKit and Agents SDK versions before production use.
Security-sensitive examples require review before copying into a public frontend or production backend.

use_cases.title: Create an internal task assistant
use_cases.description: Design a ChatKit assistant that creates, lists, updates, and completes user-specific tasks.

use_cases.title: Add ChatKit to an existing dashboard
use_cases.description: Plan the frontend widget, authenticated API calls, and backend endpoint needed for dashboard integration.

use_cases.title: Review multi-user isolation
use_cases.description: Check whether middleware, wrappers, and database filters preserve per-user data boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic ChatKit app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a simple ChatKit chatbot for a task app. Include the frontend, backend, and tool layers.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate with my backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to adapt my FastAPI app for ChatKit. Focus on the protocol endpoint, streaming response, and JWT context.

prompt_templates.title: Design MCP tool wrappers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design MCP wrapper functions for my app tools. Ensure every tool call receives the authenticated user_id.

prompt_templates.title: Audit production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my ChatKit architecture for production. Check user isolation, token handling, error handling, CORS, and deployment settings.

output_examples.input: I need a ChatKit chatbot for managing customer support tickets.
output: A layered architecture with a Next.js ChatKit panel, a FastAPI protocol endpoint, and ticket-specific MCP wrappers.
A checklist for JWT extraction, ticket ownership filters, streaming responses, and dashboard refresh behavior.

output_examples.input: My ChatKit tool creates data for the wrong user.
output: A diagnosis path that checks middleware user extraction, wrapper closure scope, and database filters.
A corrected implementation plan that keeps user_id server-side and applies it to every read and write.

output_examples.input: Prepare this ChatKit integration for deployment.
output: A deployment checklist covering domain registration, backend URL configuration, CORS, secret placement, and production token validation.
A list of security items to review before release, including frontend secrets and verbose error responses.

best_practices: Keep secrets on the backend and expose only public configuration values to the browser.
Inject user_id from validated server-side authentication context, not from request bodies or model output.
Verify user isolation with tests that use at least two separate users and conflicting resource IDs.
anti_patterns: Do not register raw MCP tools with an agent when those tools require authenticated user context.
Do not put OpenAI secret keys in NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables or browser-visible bundles.
Do not rely on polling alone for high-frequency workflows without measuring backend load.

faq.question: Does this skill include runnable source code?
faq.answer: It mainly provides documentation and implementation snippets. You must adapt the examples into your own application.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What backend stack does it target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on FastAPI, ChatKit server patterns, OpenAI Agents SDK, SQLModel-style database access, and MCP tools.

faq.question: Can it help with existing applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide endpoint design, authenticated fetch setup, tool wrapper creation, and user isolation checks.

faq.question: Is the guidance production-ready as written?
faq.answer: No. Review security-sensitive examples, dependency versions, token storage, and secret handling before production use.

faq.question: What is the main security model?
faq.answer: The skill recommends authentication middleware, per-request tool wrappers, and database filters that all use the authenticated user_id.
